old_explain: Factoring the public modulus n recovers the secret primes p and q, hence (p - 1)(q - 1) and the private exponent. Generating keys and encrypting messages would still work exactly as before; what is lost is the secrecy of the private key, which is the whole of the security.
new_explain: Factoring the public modulus n recovers the secret primes p and q, hence (p − 1)(q − 1) and a private exponent by modular inversion. Key generation and encryption can still run, but someone with those factors can recover a working private key. This is a sufficient attack; it does not prove that every way of inverting RSA is equivalent to factoring, and real encryption schemes also require suitable encodings and implementations.
